assetGroup: Standalone influenza virion, half-cutaway style - single assembled mesh (not a physically-separable piece set, despite being built from originally-separate authoring components; the delivered GLB is one continuous mesh)
componentMapping: biology > microbiology > Virus (low-level item) - ALTERNATE/companion candidate to virus-influenza-whole-nih.glb. Where that file shows the full exterior only, this file shows a half cutaway: intact spiky exterior (hemagglutinin/neuraminidase knobs) on one half, interior detail (nucleoprotein/RNA, polymerase) exposed on the other half. Matches the CLAUDE.md 3D-asset-quality-bar requirement for cross-section/cutaway support 'where applicable' (spec S13) better than any prior influenza candidate.
underlyingStructureData: Built for PathogenAR, an augmented-reality educational program from NIAID's Biovisualization Program. Depicts hemagglutinin (red/pink spikes) and neuraminidase (yellow spikes) on the envelope, with M1, M2, nucleoproteins, RNA, RNA polymerase, and other cytosolic proteins visible in the cutaway interior.
creator: kbrowne (NIAID Biovisualization Program, NIH)
attributionText: "Influenza Virion (PathogenAR)" by kbrowne, NIAID Biovisualization Program, NIH 3D (3d.nih.gov, entry 3DPX-013373). Licensed CC-BY 4.0.

validation.meshAttributes: POSITION + COLOR_0 (real per-vertex color: teal membrane, pink/red hemagglutinin spikes, yellow neuraminidase clusters, tan/purple interior nucleoprotein detail; no NORMAL attribute present)
validation.notes: Well within the 15MB hero-asset budget (6.0MB). No NORMAL accessor, same computeVertexNormals() caveat as virus-influenza-whole-nih.glb. Single continuous mesh despite the entry's own description warning the source assets have 'floating pieces... not 3D printable' - that caveat applies to the separate authoring/Unity-import files (Influenza_Virion.glb input, FBX variant), not to this specific downloaded GLB output, which validated as one mesh/one node with no structural corruption. STATUS: render-review-pending - not self-declared PASS; needs a visual-acceptance pass before any route/registry integration, and a specific check that the cutaway plane reads clearly at the app's default camera framing (not just in NIH's own thumbnail angle).
